assumptions: USD million. Parent sold machine to wholly owned subsidiary at start of year; no external sale. Remaining life five years, straight-line, zero residual; eliminate internal gain and extra depreciation. Ignore tax.

evidence.text: Parent carrying amount 100 immediately before transfer; transfer price 150.
Subsidiary records machine 150 and depreciates over five years. Parent books gain 50.
Separate EBIT totals include all stated entries; consolidated reported EBIT before elimination 240. No other adjustments.

qas.question: What gain was recorded by the parent in its own books?
qas.answer: 150−100=50 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate subsidiary depreciation after the internal transfer.
qas.answer: 150/5=30 million USD.

qas.question: Find depreciation on the original group carrying basis.
qas.answer: 100/5=20 million USD.

qas.question: Determine consolidated EBIT after both eliminations.
Why is the subsidiary's extra depreciation added back in consolidation?
qas.answer: It is depreciation on an internal gain eliminated from group carrying value; the group depreciates its original cost basis.

qas.question: Does the internal transfer generate consolidated revenue or cash from an outside buyer?
qas.answer: No. Both entities are inside the group; internal transfers are eliminated.

qas.question: Can the group's actual investing cash flows be calculated from the machine transfer?
qas.answer: No. It only describes an internal transfer; external capex and disposal flows are absent.

qas.question: Does eliminating the gain mean the parent's standalone accounting gain must also be reversed?
qas.answer: Not necessarily. The case specifies a consolidation adjustment, distinct from standalone reporting.

assumptions: USD million. Toy repo is secured borrowing; securities remain recognized. Initial collateral market value 250, cash borrowing 225; required haircut 10%. At next measurement market value falls to 210, no repayment; required collateral market value = debt/.9.

evidence.text: Securities market value 250 pledged; cash received 225 in repo.
Repo balance remains 225; collateral market value subsequently 210.
Required haircut 10%. Cash or additional securities may be posted; no interest or legal details.

qas.question: Find the haircut amount at inception.
qas.answer: 250−225=25 million USD.

qas.question: What collateral market value is required for the outstanding repo?
qas.answer: 225/.9=250 million USD.

qas.question: How much extra collateral market value is needed after the price fall?
qas.answer: 250−210=40 million USD.

qas.question: If no collateral is added, what maximum borrowing would the new collateral support at the same haircut?
qas.answer: 210×.9=189 million USD.

qas.question: Why is the 225 cash receipt not securities sales revenue?
qas.answer: The supplied accounting policy treats it as borrowing secured by retained securities.

qas.question: Can the bank treat pledged securities as fully unencumbered liquidity?
qas.answer: No. The collateral is already pledged and subject to the repo terms.

qas.question: Can actual cash margin-call settlement be determined from the 40 collateral gap?
qas.answer: No. The contract may permit cash or securities; the settlement form is not specified.

qas.question: Can the repo's annualized funding cost be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Interest and term are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy contract: service delivered immediately, unconditional payment 121 due in two years. Discount rate 10% annually; recognize revenue at PV and effective interest over time. No credit loss, cash collected only at maturity.

evidence.text: Service fully delivered January 1, contractual consideration 121 payable at end of year two.
Discount rate 10%; no variable consideration or other performance obligations.
No financing fees, default or taxes; customer pays in full on due date.

qas.question: What initial service revenue is recognized?
qas.answer: 121/1.1²=100 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate year-one interest income on the receivable.
qas.answer: 100×10%=10 million USD.

qas.question: Find the receivable carrying amount at end of year one.
qas.answer: 100+10=110 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate year-two interest income before collection.
qas.answer: 110×10%=11 million USD.

qas.question: Why is initial service revenue less than the contractual payment?
qas.answer: The payment includes financing over two years; the policy separates time value from service consideration.

qas.question: Can 121 be recorded as cash at delivery?
qas.answer: No. The payment is due in two years and no cash is received at delivery.

qas.question: Can an accounting impairment estimate be inferred from the 10% discount rate?
qas.answer: No. The discount rate is a financing input, not a disclosed default or loss estimate.

qas.question: Can the provider's margin on the service be determined?
qas.answer: No. The cost of delivering it is absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy gift cards: opening liability 45, new cash sales 70, redemption revenue 60, unused cards refunded 5, no breakage recognized. Cost of redeemed merchandise 34.

evidence.text: Opening gift card liability 45; customers buy cards for cash 70.
Cards with consideration 60 redeemed for merchandise. Cash refunds 5 for unused cards.
No breakage, other contract changes or selling expenses. Merchandise cost associated with redemptions 34.

qas.question: Find card-related cash inflow net of refunds.
qas.answer: 70−5=65 million USD.

qas.question: Compute card redemption revenue.
qas.answer: 60 million USD, corresponding to fulfilled obligations.

qas.question: Determine closing card liability.
qas.answer: 45+70−60−5=50 million USD.

qas.question: What gross profit is recognized on redeemed merchandise?
qas.answer: 60−34=26 million USD.

qas.question: Why is the unused card refund not a reduction of redemption revenue in this model?
qas.answer: The card had not been redeemed; refund reduces the deferred liability instead of revenue from fulfilled obligations.

qas.question: Does the closing liability mean 50 cash is segregated in a bank account?
qas.answer: No. A contract liability is a service obligation, not proof of ring-fenced funds.

qas.question: Can future breakage revenue be estimated?
qas.answer: No. No breakage estimates or expiry information are supplied.

qas.question: Can total retailer gross profit be computed?
qas.answer: No. Only the gift-card-related transactions are described.

assumptions: USD million. Toy deterministic future claim payments 100 at end year one and 121 at end year two; no risk margin, reinsurance or other payments. Discount at 10% base, 5% sensitivity.

evidence.text: Expected nominal claims payments: year one 100, year two 121.
Base discount 10%; alternative 5%. No changes to expected payment amounts.
No current claim payment, accounting OCI policy or capital rules provided.

qas.question: What nominal total payments are expected?
qas.answer: 100+121=221 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate the discounted liability at the 10% base rate.
Calculate the discounted liability at the 5% alternative rate.
How much does the liability rise when the discount rate falls?
Why is the lower discount rate associated with a higher liability?
qas.answer: Future payments are discounted less heavily, increasing their present value.

qas.question: Does this remeasurement change the undiscounted expected payment amounts?
qas.answer: No. They remain 100 and 121 under the stipulated sensitivity.

qas.question: Can the change be assigned to OCI rather than profit?
qas.answer: No. The presentation policy is missing.

qas.question: Can capital adequacy after the change be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Eligible capital, required capital and regulatory treatment are not provided.

assumptions: USD million. Toy joint production: shared processing cost allocated by relative sales value at split-off. Product A sales value 120, B 80. Shared cost 100; further processing A cost 18 raises its sales to 150; B sold at split-off.

evidence.text: Split-off sales values A 120, B 80; shared cost 100.
A can be processed further at incremental cost 18, final sales 150; B remains at 80.
No capacity constraints, alternative uses, tax or inventory movements.

qas.question: Allocate joint cost to product A at split-off.
Allocate joint cost to product B.
Calculate A gross profit after further processing.
qas.answer: 150−60−18=72 million USD.

qas.question: What incremental benefit does further processing A generate?
qas.answer: 150−120−18=12 million USD.

qas.question: Why is allocated joint cost irrelevant to this incremental processing decision?
qas.answer: The joint cost is incurred before split-off under either option; it cancels when comparing future revenue and cost.

qas.question: Does B's smaller allocated joint cost mean B is more profitable per unit?
qas.answer: No. Unit quantities are absent, and allocation is based on relative sales value.

qas.question: Can optimal production volume for either product be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Capacity, demand curves and marginal production costs are missing.

qas.question: Can company-wide EBIT be calculated from the joint products?
qas.answer: No. Other operating costs and business activities are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Toy project land and infrastructure cost allocated by saleable area. Two phases, 60 and 40 thousand m². Shared cost 100; phase-specific construction A 90, B 70; all Phase A sold for 210, B unsold.

evidence.text: Total saleable area 100 thousand m²: A 60, B 40; shared land/infrastructure cost 100.
Phase A construction cost 90, sold all units for 210. Phase B construction cost incurred 70, all units unsold.
No finance cost, impairment, selling expenses or tax. Allocation policy based on area.

qas.question: Calculate shared cost allocated to Phase A.
qas.answer: 100×60%=60 million USD.

qas.question: Find Phase A cost of sales after construction costs.
qas.answer: 60+90=150 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate Phase A gross profit.
qas.answer: 210−150=60 million USD.

qas.question: Determine Phase B inventory carrying amount before any impairment.
qas.answer: 40+70=110 million USD.

qas.question: Why does the land cost allocated to Phase B not enter Phase A cost of sales?
qas.answer: It relates to unsold units in B and remains in inventory under the supplied allocation rule.

qas.question: Can Phase B construction cost be expensed solely because it was paid?
qas.answer: No. The case recognizes unsold development cost as inventory; cash timing is separate.

qas.question: Can Phase B expected gross margin be estimated?
qas.answer: No. Its selling consideration and any remaining costs are unknown.

qas.question: Can the project-wide return on investment be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Sales and cash timing for B and other relevant costs are missing.

assumptions: USD million equivalent at opening rates. Toy portfolio: EUR assets 200, EUR liabilities 50, FX forward short EUR exposure 100. EUR falls 8%; linear sensitivity, forward gains offset spot change on notional. No other movements.

evidence.text: EUR assets opening USD equivalent 200, EUR liabilities equivalent 50.
Forward short EUR notional equivalent 100, no basis or transaction costs.
EUR depreciates 8% against USD. No interest, other assets or accounting classification.

qas.question: What is the unhedged net EUR position before the forward?
qas.answer: 200−50=150 million USD equivalent.

qas.question: Determine residual exposure after the forward.
qas.answer: 150−100=50 million USD equivalent long EUR.

qas.question: Find the forward gain from the currency decline.
qas.answer: 100×8%=8 million USD.

qas.question: Estimate total currency loss after the hedge.
qas.answer: −150×8%+8=−4 million USD.

qas.question: Why would hedging gross assets of 200 overstate the required hedge for net exposure?
qas.answer: EUR liabilities offset part of assets, leaving net exposure of 150 before derivatives.

qas.question: Does the partial forward hedge remove all currency exposure?
qas.answer: No. Residual long EUR exposure remains 50.

qas.question: Can the actual cash settlement date of the forward be identified?
qas.answer: No. Maturity and collateral terms are absent.

qas.question: Can the post-shock fund return be calculated from the currency loss alone?
qas.answer: No. Full NAV, other investment returns and cash flows are missing.
